tools.name: sheets.list_sheets
tools.title: List spreadsheets
tools.description: The team's spreadsheets, most recently changed first. q narrows by words in the title.

tools.name: sheets.create_sheet
tools.title: New spreadsheet
tools.description: Make a spreadsheet. Give tabs to name them, values to fill the first tab (rows of cells, typed as a person would: "$1,200", "=SUM(B2:B9)"), or template to start from an example: pipeline (Deals by stage with weighted value, a summary by stage and a chart); budget (Monthly income and costs with totals, net and a chart); hiring (Candidates by role and stage, with a pivot table of the pipeline).

values.description: Rows of cells for the first tab, from A1

tools.name: sheets.get_sheet
tools.title: Open a spreadsheet
tools.description: One spreadsheet: its tabs (with the range in use, frozen rows, filter and any CRM or pivot link), charts, open comments, sharing and address. Read cells with sheets.read_range.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.rename_sheet
tools.title: Rename a spreadsheet
tools.description: Change a spreadsheet's title.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.copy_sheet
tools.title: Make a copy
tools.description: Copy a spreadsheet with everything in it (tabs, formulas, formats, charts, comments) into your workspace. Give sheet for one of the team's, or share_token for one someone shared with a view-only link. The copy is not shared.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

share_token.description: The token at the end of a view-only link (/v/<token>)

tools.name: sheets.delete_sheet
tools.title: Delete a spreadsheet
tools.description: Delete a spreadsheet for everyone on the team. It disappears from the list and its share link stops working. An agent calling this asks a person first.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.read_range
tools.title: Read cells
tools.description: Exact cell contents: values (numbers stay numbers, errors are their code like #DIV/0!) and, where a cell has one, its formula. Leave range out to read everything in use on the tab. text: true adds what each cell shows (formatted, like $1,200.00); formats: true adds each cell's format. version reads an earlier version (sheets.list_versions).

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

range.description: A1 notation: B3, A1:D20, A:C (whole columns), 2:5 (whole rows), or 'Tab name'!A1:B9

version.description: A version id, to read the spreadsheet as it was then

tools.name: sheets.write_range
tools.title: Write cells
tools.description: Write rows of cells starting at the top-left of range. Cells are read as a person typing them: "1200" and "$1,200" are numbers, "12%" is 0.12, "2026-10-07" is a date, "=SUM(B2:B9)" is a formula, "'007" stays text. input: "raw" stores strings exactly as text instead; "exact" stores contents as Sheets keeps them (what sheets.read_range formulas and values give back: a formula starts with =, text starting with ' shows without it), for copying cells exactly. null clears a cell. Returns the values the cells came to, and any formula errors.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

range.description: Where to start (default A1), or the whole range

formats.description: Formats for the same cells: b, i, u, s, fc (text colour), bg (fill), ha (align), wrap, nf (number format code), fs (size). null clears.

tools.name: sheets.set_formula
tools.title: Set a formula
tools.description: Put a formula in a cell, like =SUMIF(B2:B20,"Won",C2:C20). fill copies it across a range the way dragging the fill handle does: relative references move, $absolute ones stay (fill: "D2:D20" from cell D2). Checks the formula first and returns what it came to.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

formula.description: The formula, with or without the leading =

fill.description: A range that includes the cell, to fill the formula into

tools.name: sheets.append_rows
tools.title: Add rows
tools.description: Add rows under the last row in use (or under the table that starts at range, like A1). Cells are read as typed, as in sheets.write_range.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

range.description: The table's first cell or range, when the tab holds more than one table

tools.name: sheets.clear_range
tools.title: Clear cells
tools.description: Empty a range: what: values (default), formats or all.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

range.description: A1 notation: B3, A1:D20, A:C (whole columns), 2:5 (whole rows), or 'Tab name'!A1:B9

tools.name: sheets.find
tools.title: Find
tools.description: Find cells by what they show (or by their formula, with formulas: true), across every tab or one. Returns each match's tab, cell, value and formula.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

tools.name: sheets.sort
tools.title: Sort
tools.description: Sort the rows of a range (default: everything in use) by one or more columns. A header row is kept on top (found automatically; header: true or false to say). Formulas in moved rows keep pointing at their own row, as in Excel. Empty cells go last.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

range.description: A1 notation: B3, A1:D20, A:C (whole columns), 2:5 (whole rows), or 'Tab name'!A1:B9

column.description: A letter (C), a header from the first row ("Amount"), or a number counting from 1 within the range
A letter (C), a header from the first row ("Amount"), or a number counting from 1 within the range

tools.name: sheets.filter
tools.title: Filter
tools.description: Turn on the tab's filter (everyone sees it, as in Google Sheets) and set a condition on one column; rows that do not match are hidden. Call again for more columns. clear: true removes the filter. Returns the rows that still show. To look without changing what others see, use sheets.read_range or sheets.find.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

range.description: The table, header row first (default: everything in use)

op.description: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains, not_contains, starts_with, empty, not_empty, in (with values), or all (no condition)

tools.name: sheets.insert_rows
tools.title: Insert rows
tools.description: Insert rows before row at (counting from 1). Every formula that points past them moves.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

tools.title: Delete rows

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.create_chart
tools.title: Add a chart
tools.description: A chart from a range, drawn on the tab and kept up to date. type: column, bar, line, area, pie, scatter. By columns (default) the first column is the labels and each other column a series named by its header; series_by: "rows" turns that around. series picks which columns (letters) or rows (numbers) to plot. at is the cell where its top-left corner sits. Returns the chart with the data it shows.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

range.description: A1 notation: B3, A1:D20, A:C (whole columns), 2:5 (whole rows), or 'Tab name'!A1:B9

tools.title: Change a chart

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.description: Remove a chart. Its data stays.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

tools.name: sheets.create_pivot
tools.title: Pivot table
tools.description: Summarise a table on a new tab: one row per value of rows (a header or letter), optional columns to split across, and values to work out (summarize: sum, count, average, min, max of a field). It is written as live formulas (SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, ...), so it updates as the table changes and opens in Excel. sheets.refresh_link picks up new categories.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: The tab with the table

range.description: The table, header row first (default: everything in use)

tools.name: sheets.import_xlsx
tools.title: Import an Excel file
tools.description: Bring in an .xlsx file (as base64) as a new spreadsheet: values, formulas, formats, frozen panes, widths, notes and named ranges. Returns an honest report: what carried over, what did not (merged cells, conditional formatting, charts, macros, ...), and every formula whose result differs from what the file saved.

name.description: The file name, used as the title when there is none

tools.name: sheets.import_csv
tools.title: Import CSV
tools.description: Bring in CSV text (or base64). With sheet, it goes on a new tab of that spreadsheet (or replaces tab); without, it becomes a new spreadsheet. Numbers, money, percents and dates are read as such. The delimiter (comma, semicolon or tab) is found automatically.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: Replace this tab's contents

name.description: Name for the new tab or spreadsheet

tools.name: sheets.export
tools.title: Download
tools.description: Download a spreadsheet as .xlsx (every tab, with formulas and their results, formats, frozen panes and comments as notes) or one tab as .csv (what the cells show; values: "raw" for plain numbers). Returns a download link; content: true also returns the file as base64. Says what an .xlsx cannot carry (charts, for now).

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tab.description: A tab, by name or id (default: the first tab). A range like 'Deals'!A1:C9 names its own tab.

content.description: Also return the file as base64

tools.name: sheets.export_data
tools.title: Export everything
tools.description: Every spreadsheet on the team in one zip: each as .xlsx, plus sheets.json with every tab, cell, format, chart and comment exactly as stored. Your data is never stuck here.

tools.name: sheets.import_from_crm
tools.title: Pull from the CRM
tools.description: Pull CRM records onto a tab, kept linked so sheets.refresh_link brings it up to date. kind: deals, contacts, leads, organizations, activities (with the usual fields), or soql for any read-only query, like SELECT Name, StageName, Amount FROM Opportunity WHERE StageName != 'Lost'. Uses the CRM's own tools (crm.query), as you. Formulas beside the table keep working after a refresh.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

fields.description: CRM field names, like Name, Amount, CloseDate, Account.Name

tab.description: Replace this tab instead of adding one

tools.name: sheets.refresh_link
tools.title: Refresh
tools.description: Bring a linked tab up to date: a CRM tab pulls its records again; a pivot tab is rebuilt from its table (new categories appear). Without tab, every linked tab in the spreadsheet.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.connect_crm
tools.title: Connect the CRM
tools.description: Standalone servers: where the wOS CRM is (its address) and an access token from it (crm.create_access_token, read only is enough). disconnect: true forgets it. Inside the wOS suite nothing is needed: Sheets uses the CRM app directly.

tools.name: sheets.share
tools.title: Share a link
tools.description: link: "view" makes a read-only link anyone can open without an account (it shows values and charts, never lets them edit). link: "off" stops it. Everyone on the team can already open and edit every spreadsheet. An agent turning a link on asks a person first.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.list_versions
tools.title: Version history
tools.description: Earlier versions of a spreadsheet, newest first: one is kept automatically every ten minutes of editing, plus every named version. Read one with sheets.read_range version, or bring it back with sheets.restore_version.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.save_version
tools.title: Name this version
tools.description: Save the spreadsheet as it is now, with a name, so it is easy to find in the history.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.restore_version
tools.title: Restore a version
tools.description: Bring back an earlier version for everyone. Nothing is lost: the version before the restore is saved first, so it can be restored too.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title

tools.name: sheets.sync
tools.title: Catch up
tools.description: For screens: the changes to a spreadsheet that a copy at state_vector (base64 Yjs state vector; empty for everything) has not seen, as one base64 Yjs update. Agents use sheets.read_range instead.

sheet.description: The spreadsheet: its id (wb_...) or its exact title
